data.reasoning: The deepseek model successfully reviewed all 4 files (.SRCINFO, .gitignore, LICENSE, PKGBUILD) and found no malicious indicators. The PKGBUILD is a standard Go package build script that downloads a pinned tarball from the official GitHub release with a SHA256 checksum, uses standard Go tooling, and performs only normal packaging operations (adjusting systemd service file paths). The qwen model's inconclusive result was due to API errors (HTTP 400) preventing it from reviewing 3 of 4 files, not from finding any security issues. The files that qwen failed to review (.gitignore, LICENSE, .SRCINFO) are standard metadata files with no executable code, and deepseek confirmed they are benign.
data.disagreement_analysis: The disagreement stems from infrastructure failure, not analytical disagreement. The qwen model encountered HTTP 400 BadRequestError when attempting to audit .gitignore, LICENSE, and .SRCINFO, leaving it unable to render a complete verdict. The deepseek model successfully audited all files and found them safe. There is no substantive disagreement about the package's safety.
coverage_issues: qwen model failed to review 3/4 files (.gitignore, LICENSE, .SRCINFO) due to HTTP 400 API errors, resulting in an incomplete audit
learnings: Implement retry logic or fallback models when LLM API calls fail with transient errors (HTTP 400/500) to prevent incomplete audits from being marked inconclusive
When a model fails to review files due to API errors, the audit tool should distinguish between 'files reviewed and found safe' vs 'files not reviewed due to errors' in the final verdict calculation

For packages with only standard metadata files (.gitignore, LICENSE, .SRCINFO) plus a PKGBUILD, a single successful PKGBUILD review may be sufficient for a safe verdict if the metadata files are trivially non-executable
